topics.title: Useful but Harmful Insects Primary 2 (Basic 2) - Home Economics
topics.content:
AGRICULTURE
PREVOCATIONAL STUDIES
SECOND TERM
WEEK 6
PRIMARY 2
THEME - PROTECTION ISSUES IN AGRICULTURE
PREVIOUS LESSON - Usefulness of Insects Primary 2 (Basic 2) - Agriculture
TOPIC - USEFUL INSECTS
LEARNING AREA
1. Introductory Activities
2. Useful but Harmful Insects
3. Lesson Evaluation and Weekly Assessment (Test)
PERFORMANCE OBJECTIVES
By the end of the lesson, most should have attained the following objectives (cognitive, affective and psychomotor) and should be able to -
state the useful but harmful insects.
ENTRY BEHAVIOUR
The pupils can identify harmful farms insects.
INSTRUCTIONAL MATERIALS
The teacher will teach the lesson with the aid of:
1. Honey
2. Chart or sample of useful insects
3. Insect nets
METHOD OF TEACHING
Choose a suitable and appropriate methods for the lessons.
Note - Irrespective of choosing methods of teaching, always introduce an activities that will arouse pupil’s interest or lead them to the lessons.
REFERENCE MATERIALS
1. Scheme of Work
2. 9 - Years Basic Education Curriculum
3. Course Book
4. All Relevant Material
5. Online Information
WRITING INSTRUCTION
Copy as I write or draw as I write. This instruction should be given when you need the pupils to write or draw.
CONTENT OF THE LESSON
LESSON 1 - INTRODUCTORY ACTIVITIES
Teacher’s Activities - Ask pupils if they have beaten by any Insects. If yes, let them describe how they feel by the bit.
Pupil’s Activities - Very painful, etc.
Teacher’s Activities - Listen to the pupil’s discussion.
Teacher’s remarks - Listen to the pupils and give them a great cheer for expressing their feelings. Discuss with the pupils, some useful but harmful insects.
USEFUL BUT HARMFUL INSECTS
Useful insects but harmful are insects are useful and dangerous to plants, animals and people.
These insects kill and eat the other insects including harmful insects.
Some of the USEFUL insects are very harmful and dangerous, for example - honey bees.
They are dangerous to people, plants and animals. This is because, they can kill people, animals and eat up the farm crops.
COMMON USEFUL BUT HARMFUL INSECTS
1. Bees
2. Termites
3. Ants
4. Tsetse fly
5. Tick
6. Mosquito
7. Scorpion
8. Soldier ant, etc.
LESSON 2 - REVISION AND WEEKLY ASSESSMENT
As stated in performance objectives or lesson evaluation.
PRESENTATION
To deliver the lesson, the teacher adopts the following steps:
1. To introduce the lesson, the teacher revises the previous lesson. Based on this, he/she asks the pupils some questions;
2. Displays and identify preserved or use samples or listed insects.
Pupil’s Activities - Observe closely and identify useful insects.
3. Asks pupils to separate the harmful ones among other insects.
Pupil’s Activities - Identify harmful insects and describe the pain caused by these insects.
4. Summarizes the lesson on the board.
Pupil’s Activities - Copy as the teacher writes.
5. Assignment - Find out harmful insects at home.
CONCLUSION
To conclude the lesson for the week, the teacher revises the entire lesson and links it to the following week’s lesson.
NEXT LESSON
Harmful Insects at Home Primary 2 (Basic 2) - Agriculture
LESSON EVALUATION
Ask pupils to name two insects that are useful but can be harmful.
WEEKLY ASSESSMENT
ANSWER ALL THE QUESTIONS
1. Useful insects are insects are useful to _________________.
A. Crops, animals and people
B. crops, animals and air
C. Crops, animals insects
2. _________________ are insects are useful to crops and people.
A. Useful farm animals
B. Useful farmers
C. Useful farm insects
State 3 useful farm insects but harmful.
3. _________________
4. _________________
5. _________________

topics.title: Uses and Cares of Bedroom as a Functional Room in the Home Primary 2 (Basic 2) - Home Economics
topics.content:
HOME ECONOMICS
PREVOCATIONAL STUDIES
SECOND TERM
WEEK 8
PRIMARY 2
THEME - THE HOME
PREVIOUS LESSON - Uses and Cares of Dining Room as a Functional Room in the Home Primary 2 (Basic 2) - Home Economics
TOPIC - THE HOME
LEARNING AREA
1. Introductory Activities
2. Description of Bedroom
3. Uses and Cares of Bedroom as a Functional Room in the Home
4. Revision and Weekly Assessment (Test)
PERFORMANCE OBJECTIVES
By the end of the lesson, most of the pupils should have attained the following objectives (cognitive, affective and psychomotor) and should be able to -
1. list the number of functional rooms in their homes.
2. describe the bedroom.
3. state the uses and cares of bedroom.
ENTRY BEHAVIOUR
The pupils can identify the bedroom.
INSTRUCTIONAL MATERIALS
The teacher will teach the lesson with the aid of pictures and charts showing functional Rooms (dining room) in the Home.
METHOD OF TEACHING
Choose a suitable and appropriate methods for the lessons.
Note - Irrespective of choosing methods of teaching, always introduce an activities that will arouse pupil’s interest or lead them to the lessons.
REFERENCE MATERIALS
1. Scheme of Work
2. 9 - Years Basic Education Curriculum
3. Course Book
4. All Relevant Material
5. Online Information
WRITING INSTRUCTION
Copy as I write or draw as I write. This instruction should be given when you need the pupils to write or draw.
CONTENT OF THE LESSON
INTRODUCTORY ACTIVITIES
Teacher’s Activities - Display a chart showing different parts of a home for pupils to identify the bedroom and describe.
Pupil’s Responses - This is a bedroom room. It is the room where we rest and sleep.
Teacher’s remark - Home a house or apartment where people lives as a family. It has many rooms. Bedroom is one of the rooms in the home. Based on the previous assignment, discuss the uses and cares of bedroom. Write on the board, the contents of discussion.
DESCRIPTION OF BEDROOM
A bedroom is a room in the home where we rest and sleep.
There are different types of bedrooms, namely -
1. Master bedroom
- Master bedroom is for our parents - papa and mama.
2. Children bedrooms
- Children rooms are mainly for children like you.
3. Guest room
- Guest rooms are for people that came for visits.
LESSON 2 - USES OF BEDROOMS AS A FUNCTIONAL ROOMS IN THE HOME
The uses of bedrooms are -
1. It is used for resting.
2. It is used for relaxation.
3. It is used for sleeping.
CARES OF BEDROOMS AS A FUNCTIONAL ROOMS IN THE HOME
1. Remove the cobwebs.
2. Sweep the floor regularly.
3. Clean the be and beddings.
4. Always put fresh
5. Make the bed.
6. Arrange other things in bedroom back to their place.
QUICK ASSESSMENT
Ask pupils to -
1. Describe the Kitchen.
2. state the uses and cares of kitchen.
ASSIGNMENT
Find out -
1. The meaning of bedroom.
2. The uses and cares of bedroom.
PRESENTATION
To deliver the lesson, the teacher adopts the following steps:
1. To introduce the lesson, the teacher revises the previous lesson. Based on this, he/she asks the pupils some questions;
2. Displays charts or pictures of functional rooms in the home.
Pupil’s Activities - Identify and describe the bedroom.
3. Discusses the uses and cares of Bedroom.
Pupil’s Activities - State the uses and cares of Bedroom.
4. Summarizes the lesson on the board.
Pupil’s  Activities - Copy as the teacher writes.
CONCLUSION
To conclude the lesson for the week, the teacher revises the entire lesson and links it to the following week’s lesson.
NEXT LESSON
Uses and Cares of kitchen and Store as a Functional Room in the Home Primary 2 (Basic 2) - Home Economics
LESSON EVALUATION
Ask pupils to:
1. state the number of functional rooms they have in their homes.
2. describe the bedroom.
3. state and describe types of bedrooms.
4. state the uses and cares of bedroom as a functional room in their home.
WORKBOOK ASSESSMENT
(WEEKLY TEST)
1. _______________ a house or apartment where people lives as a family.
A. Home
B. Bedroom
C. Kitchen
2. There are _______ functional rooms in the home.
A. 5
B. 6
C. 7
3. _______________ is a room where we rest, relax and sleep.
A. Sitting room
B. Bedroom
C. Dining room
4. There are ________ types of bedrooms.
A. 1
B. 2
C. 3

A. Guest rooms
B. Children rooms
C. Master bedroom

A. Guest rooms
B. Children rooms
C. Master bedroom
7. _______________ is mainly for the kids.
A. Guest rooms
B. Children rooms
C. Master bedroom

A. resting, relaxing and sleeping
B. resting, bathing and eating

9. Say Yes/No or circle the items found in bedroom.
- Gas cooker
- Bedding

CONTENT OF THE LESSON

Teacher’s Activities - Display a chart showing different parts of a home for pupils to identify and describe the Kitchen and the store.
Pupil’s Responses - This is a kitchen and store. Kitchen is the room where we cooked our food. Store is where we keep our foodstuff.
Teacher’s remark - Home a house or apartment where people lives as a family. It has many rooms. Kitchen and Store are also rooms in the home. Based on the previous assignment, discuss the uses and cares of kitchen and store. Write on the board, the contents of discussion.
DESCRIPTION OF KITCHEN AND STORE
KITCHEN
A kitchen is a part of the room where we cook and prepare our food.
STORE
Store is a room mostly inside the kitchen where we keep our foodstuff, utensils and other kitchen equipments.
LESSON 2 - USES OF KITCHEN AND STORE AS A FUNCTIONAL ROOMS IN THE HOME
Kitchen is used for cooking and preparing our food.
Store is used for keeping our foodstuff and other kitchen equipments.
CARES OF KITCHEN AS A FUNCTIONAL ROOMS IN THE HOME
KITCHEN
1. Wash all utensils after use.
2. Put all utensils in their place.
3. Sweep the kitchen regularly.
4. Remove the cobwebs.
5. Dust all the kitchen equipments.
STORE
1. Sweep the floor.
2. Remove the cobwebs.
3. Arrange the foodstuff and equipments.
QUICK ASSESSMENT

1. differentiate between the Kitchen and the store.
2. state the uses and cares of kitchen and store.
ASSIGNMENT

1. The meaning of bathroom and toilet.
2. The uses and cares of bathroom and toilet..

TOILET

There are different types of toilets - private and visitor toilets.
Private toilets are attached to different bedrooms in the home While visitor toilet is attached to the sitting or at the entrance of the sitting.
LESSON 2 - USES OF KITCHEN AND STORE AS A FUNCTIONAL ROOMS IN THE HOME

topics.title: Uses of Items Found in the Home and Position where Each Item are Kept Primary 2 (Basic 2) - Home Economics
topics.content:
HOME ECONOMICS
PREVOCATIONAL STUDIES
SECOND TERM
WEEK 11
PRIMARY 2
THEME - THE HOME
PREVIOUS LESSON - Uses and Cares of Bathroom and Toilet as a Functional Room in the Home Primary 2 (Basic 2) - Home Economics
TOPIC - THE HOME
LEARNING AREA
1. Introductory Activities
2. Items Found in the Rooms in the Home
3. Where Items Found in the Rooms in the Home Kept
4. Revision and Weekly Assessment (Test)
PERFORMANCE OBJECTIVES
By the end of the lesson, the pupils should have attained the following objectives (cognitive, affective and psychomotor) and should be able to -
1. list the number of functional rooms in their homes.
2. state the uses of the rooms in their homes.
3. mention the uses of the items found in the rooms in their homes.
4. identify where the different items found in the home are kept.
ENTRY BEHAVIOUR
The pupils can identify and state the uses of Items found in the home.
INSTRUCTIONAL MATERIALS
The teacher will teach the lesson with the aid of pictures and charts showing functional rooms in the home, items found in the home.
METHOD OF TEACHING
Choose a suitable and appropriate methods for the lessons.
Note - Irrespective of choosing methods of teaching, always introduce an activities that will arouse pupil’s interest or lead them to the lessons.
REFERENCE MATERIALS
1. Scheme of Work
2. 9 - Years Basic Education Curriculum
3. Course Book
4. All Relevant Material
5. Online Information
WRITING INSTRUCTION
Copy as I write or draw as I write. This instruction should be given when you need the pupils to write or draw.
CONTENT OF THE LESSON
INTRODUCTORY ACTIVITIES
Teacher’s Activities - Display a chart showing different parts of a home for pupils to identify and state the uses of different rooms in the home.
Pupil’s Activities - The sitting room, bedroom, dining room, etc.
Teacher’s remark - Each room in the home are known as functional room. They served different purpose. Each room has items that make them functional. Write on the board each room mentioned by the pupils and ask them to the items found the rooms.
FUNCTIONAL ROOMS IN THE HOME
Home a house or apartment where people lives as a family. The following are the rooms in the home.
1. Sitting/Living room
2. Bedrooms - (Master and Visitor’s or Guest’s rooms)
3. Dining rooms
4. Bathroom
5. Toilets (Master’s and Visitor’s or Guest’s toilets)
6. Kitchen
7. Store
LESSON 2 - USES OF ITEMS FOUND IN THE HOME AND WHERE EACH ARE KEPT
Teacher’s/Pupil’s Activities - Discuss each item found in the functional rooms in the home and its uses and where it is kept.
1. Set of chairs
- Uses - For sitting and relaxation
- Position to keep - Sitting room.
2. Bed
- Uses - For sleeping
- Position to keep - Bedrooms.
3. Bucket/basin
- Uses - For fetching water and washing clothes and plates.
- Position to keep - Kitchen, toilet and bathrooms.
4. Gas cooker/Kerosene stove
- Uses - For cooking
- Position to keep - Kitchen.
5. Plates, cups and cutleries
- Uses - For eating and drinking
- Position to keep - Kitchen and dining room.
6. Table
- Uses - For eating and writing
- Position to keep - Kitchen, dining room and sitting room.
7. Television, dstv, gotv or startime and radio set
- Uses - For entertainment and news
- Position to keep - Sitting room.
8. Air conditioning, ceiling or standing fan
- Uses - For cooling
- Position to keep - Sitting room and bedrooms.
9. Water heater
- Uses - For cooking and bath
- Position to keep - Kitchen and bathrooms.
10. Freezer and refrigerator
- Uses - For preservation and cooling
- Position to keep - Kitchen and dinning room.
PRESENTATION
To deliver the lesson, the teacher adopts the following steps:
1. To introduce the lesson, the teacher revises the previous lesson. Based on this, he/she asks the pupils some questions;
2. Displays charts or pictures of functional rooms in the home.
Pupil’s Activities - Identify charts or pictures of functional rooms in the home.
3. Discuss the uses of each of the functional rooms in the home.
Pupil’s Activities - Discuss the number of functional rooms in the homes.
4. Discuss each item found in the functional rooms in the home and its uses and where it is kept.
Pupil’s Activities - Indicate what the rooms in their houses are used for. Also, mention the uses of the different items/objects found in the home.
5. Teacher’s/Pupil’s Activities - Bring pictures of house.
6. Summarizes the lesson on the board.
Pupil’s  Activities - Copy as the teacher writes.
CONCLUSION
To conclude the lesson for the week, the teacher revises the entire lesson and links it to the following week’s lesson.
NEXT LESSON
Revision and Second Term Examination Home Economics Primary 2 (Basic 2) - Home Economics work in progress
LESSON EVALUATION
Ask pupils to:
1. state the number of functional rooms they have in their homes.
2. state the uses of each the functional rooms in their home.
3. mention the uses of four items found In the home.
4. state where any four items in a functional room may be found.
WORKBOOK ASSESSMENT
(WEEKLY TEST)
1. Television, radio set, dstv, gotv and startime are items found __________.
A. sitting room
B. bedrooms
